title: Lamb keema with new potatoes and cabbage

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole ingredient or a plain cupboard staple such as tinned tomatoes, garam masala and natural yoghurt.

supermarket.reason: Lamb mince, pointed cabbage, new potatoes and the spices are everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a casserole with a lid and a wooden spoon, and the technique is simple browning and simmering.

works.reason: 500g lamb mince, 500g potatoes, a whole cabbage and peas in a tin of tomatoes plus 300ml water make a well-sauced keema for four, and halved new potatoes will be tender after 20 minutes.

honest_times.reason: 25 minutes covers slicing onions, halving potatoes, shredding cabbage and 10 minutes of browning, and the 20 plus 8 minutes of simmering roughly matches the 35 minutes of cook time.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, nothing unlisted appears apart from water, and 'coriander' matches the fresh coriander id.

seasonal_feel.reason: A whole pointed cabbage goes in alongside new potatoes and peas, so it is a main component rather than a garnish, and a light keema suits late May.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a balanced family dinner of lamb, potatoes, cabbage and peas with no added sugar.
